The tribe is fighting the project in federal court and has erected “no trespassing” signs to keep border wall contractors off its land. As ProPublica recently reported, DHS has responded by deploying masked federal agents as escorts for its work crews and conducting aerial surveillance of tribal members. The head of CBP has justified the need for a wall by describing the reservation as “one of the most dangerous smuggling and trafficking corridors on the Southwest border.”
Verlon M. Jose, the tribe’s chairman, expressed gratitude that the park service had notified his office of the discovery, but mourned the fact that it was necessary.
“When you have mass destruction and disturbance of land taking place where there are clearly sacred sites, cemeteries and other areas of cultural importance, these types of discoveries are bound to happen,” Jose said in a statement. “Every time this happens it is a wound to the heart of all members of the Tohono O’odham Nation — these are our ancestors, our family members — whose remains are being desecrated.”
U.S. Rep. Adelita Grijalva, who appeared with Eiler and the chairman at the August news conference, blasted the government for failing to heed their warnings. “Tribal leaders and elders have warned DHS about the devastating consequences of bulldozing through their ancestral lands, beginning with the destruction of the Las Playas Intaglio,” she said in a statement. “For months, those warnings have fallen on deaf ears. Now, we are seeing exactly what they feared: sacred sites destroyed and ancestral burial grounds desecrated.”
James T. Watson, curator of bioarcheology in the Arizona State Museum at the University of Arizona, analyzed the remains recovered in Organ Pipe in the field.
While he was not authorized to discuss the details of his findings without park service approval, Watson said in an email that he confirmed the remains were human. The evidence suggested they were cremated in a manner consistent with precolonial practices in the region dating back 1,500 years, he wrote.
Under NAGPRA, the graves protection act, Native American remains inadvertently uncovered on park service lands must be immediately secured, Watson explained, and the superintendent of the jurisdiction must notify “all relevant lineal descendants” with “potential cultural affiliation or ancestral ties to the land.”
“Work in the immediate discovery area must remain suspended for at least 30 calendar days,” he wrote, while the park service consults with tribal representatives “to determine the disposition and physical treatment of the remains.”
In a region as rich with archaeological sites as the American Southwest, the inadvertent disturbance of Native American remains occurs with some regularity. What sets the discovery in Organ Pipe apart are the extraordinary powers the Department of Homeland Security wields to expedite wall construction in the borderlands.
Following the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, Congress passed the Real ID Act, which included a provision empowering the secretary of DHS to waive any law that might slow border wall construction. In the two decades since, DHS has invoked its powers 66 times, with 60 of those instances occurring under President Donald Trump’s two administrations.
When DHS uses this authority, it typically waives dozens of laws at a time. That was the case in 2019 when the department set its sights on Organ Pipe. A waiver issued by then-acting Secretary Kevin K. McAleenan set aside more than 40 of the nation’s most stringent environmental and cultural resource protection laws, including the National Environmental Policy Act, the Endangered Species Act, the Clean Water Act and others. Also on that list was the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act, the landmark 1990 law that acknowledged the nation’s long history of desecrating Native American burials and required that ancestral remains and cultural objects be returned to tribes.
In an internal 2019 report obtained by The Washington Post, park service officials identified nearly two dozen archaeological sites in Organ Pipe as at risk of damage or total destruction by government contractors.
Of particular significance is a desert oasis known as Quitobaquito Springs. Less than 200 feet from the international border, the springs provide one of the only reliable sources of groundwater and shade for miles around, and they were a longtime gathering place, grazing site and home for O’odham families.
“Archaeological evidence of human presence at Quitobaquito extends back thousands of years, at least to Archaic times,” the survey found, adding that the springs represent the “only known Hia C-ed O’odham village site in the United States.”
A park service report in 2024 noted that a cemetery at Quitobaquito holds the remains of at least two families, including Eiler’s, and 34 graves. Throughout the region, remains of 5,500 ancestors that were displaced have been made available for return to the Tohono O’odham Nation, according to ProPublica’s NAGPRA database.
“This sort of incident has happened numerous times across our homeland, and it’s always alarming to hear about a case from an O’odham point of view,” said David Martínez, a professor of American Indian and transborder studies at the University of Arizona and a member of the Hia-Ced O’odham and Akimel O’odham tribes, as well as the Gila River Indian Community.
“Those remains shouldn’t have been disturbed in the first place,” he said. “While there are protocols existing today to properly care for these remains, ultimately, whatever either the government or the corporate world is pursuing to build, we know that at some juncture that construction will continue, and it always leaves us feeling, I think, a little hollow.”
Today, Quitobaquito lies in the shadow of the border wall erected during Trump’s first term. Its construction required detonating explosives in the national monument, blasting apart an area called Monument Hill and outraging tribal leaders. According to Eiler, the remains recovered in September were not found at the springs, though government work crews are working in close proximity to the site.
This year, DHS hired Sundt Construction, an Arizona-based company, to build a second wall in the monument. The $443 million contract was finalized in May. (Sundt directed questions concerning the discovery of human remains on its job site to CBP.)
According to CBP, the 2019 waiver for Organ Pipe is still in effect, years after completion of the project that prompted it. A second waiver, exempting DHS from many of the same laws and applying to the national monument as well as a wildlife refuge to the west, was issued by Homeland Security’s then-Secretary Kristi Noem last year.
“Unfortunately, there is no end date to the effectiveness of the waivers,” said Dinah Bear, a Tucson-based lawyer who served for 25 years as a senior attorney in the White House’s Council on Environmental Quality under both Democratic and Republican administrations. What’s more, she added, “there’s nothing in the statutory language that ties the waivers to a particular project.”
The Department of Homeland Security’s waiver powers have been central to a high-profile legal fight over the department’s efforts to build a border wall through Big Bend National Park in West Texas, with a federal judge overseeing the case recently ordering a temporary halt to the project.
Borderlands advocates in Arizona are hoping for similar interventions. In Congress, Grijalva is preparing legislation to void existing waivers that have allowed DHS to disregard laws designed to protect tribal sovereignty, sacred sites and environmentally sensitive lands.
In the meantime, construction on the border continues. For Eiler, it’s not just the destruction in Organ Pipe that’s troubling. She sees the disturbance of tribal graves resulting from wall construction as reflective of a wider pattern of destruction across the border.
“It’s sad because it’s not only happening down there,” she said. “It’s happening all over the United States, and nobody’s saying much about it.”

theintercept.com.title: Warnings About ICE at the Polls Risk Their Own Kind of Voter Suppression
theintercept.com.text:
Anxiety over ICE at the polls is a double-edged sword for the Trump administration: There’s the fear that federal immigration agents will illegally descend on voters, and there’s the threat that by boosting awareness of that fear, activists and journalists will help the federal government carry out the work of voter intimidation.
“Even just rumors of [ICE at the polls] are going to spread fear. That’s not what we want,” said Daniela Padilla, deputy director at Texas for All, a statewide coalition of organizations working on democracy and justice issues. “Even your reporting around, ‘We’re watching for ICE at the polls’ — it could scare voters.”
In Texas, a 40 percent Latino state where a longtime Republican grip on power now finds itself in question, there are real concerns that Immigrations and Customs Enforcement agents could pop up in targeted communities to make people afraid to go out and vote on Tuesday. But while the possibility of election interference has been discussed as one of several “big ticket items” of this year’s midterms, Padilla said, “the biggest threat that we face in Texas this year is voter suppression.”
That suppression can take many forms. In Tarrant County, for example, where local officials closed 92 polling locations, reports from early voting indicated some election officials wrongly turned away eligible voters. More than fearing ICE would actually approach the polls, Padilla and several organizers working on election integrity and voting rights in Texas told The Intercept they were worried that journalists amplifying the Trump administration’s stated plans to “surround the polls” with ICE and federal agents could function as an inadvertent form of voter suppression.
Federal and state law prohibits federal immigration agents from being inside polling sites and bar any form of voter intimidation. Those laws haven’t stopped the Trump administration and its allies from threatening to deploy ICE and military personnel around the country during elections. In August, the Department of Justice announced that it planned to send at least 1,000 federal monitors to oversee midterm voting, prompting multiple states to assert they would not let them inside polling locations. As states like Maine prepared to respond to the federal presence at the polls, the DOJ claimed to Newsweek it “never said” it would send federal law enforcement to the polls.
“The Trump administration has been spreading fear for months, refusing to say that they will not send ICE to the polls,” said Emily French, policy director at Common Cause Texas. “I think that the main function of this discussion around ICE at the polls from the Trump administration is scaring people into staying home on Election Day.”
According to Brianna Brown, executive director of the Texas Organizing Project, disinformation efforts are a common voter-suppression tactic in Texas. “So we’re trying to reassure people it’s safe to vote,” she said.
Texas is home to one of the most dramatic potential Senate upsets in the country, with Democratic state Rep. James Talarico leading in the polls over the state’s scandal-plagued Republican attorney general Ken Paxton in a race that could see Texas end up with a Democratic senator for the first time since the ’90s. And the 32 million-person state has enough voter suppression strategies even without ICE in the picture, Brown said, pointing to a 2021 bill that banned drive-through voting, weakened protections for disabled voters, and gave more power to poll watchers appointed on behalf of a candidate or political party.
“Texas is just like a perfect storm,” Brown said.
When ICE showed up at a polling site in San Antonio in May — marking the first known case of ICE at the polls in the country during this year’s primaries — the county sheriff kicked the agents out. Even then, it did not appear that the federal agents were targeting someone in the process of voting; they had arrived at the scene shortly after state police, with whom they work closely, pulled someone over in the polling site’s parking lot.
That day, staff at the Texas Organizing Project and a group of civil and voting rights organizations working as part of the Texas Election Protection coalition helped coordinate outreach to the local sheriff to get ICE removed from the site.
The state coalition is part of a nationwide effort to protect this year’s elections from interference — federal or otherwise. In Texas, the Lawyers’ Committee and several other groups including the Barbara Jordan Leadership Institute, Common Cause Texas, and the Texas Civil Rights Project have been training people to help make sure voters know their rights on Election Day and that they report any instances of voter intimidation — whether an eligible voter is wrongly turned away or someone spots ICE — to a national hotline.
“We want to inform people, but we don’t want to scare them from coming to the polls,” said Khanay Turner-Osborne, executive director of the Barber Jordan Leadership Institute. She said she hasn’t heard much concern about ICE showing up around polling sites in Tarrant County, where she’s based and where people can vote at any polling site in the county. But still, for voters in hotspots of ICE activity and other forms of voter suppression, the group has told them to consider voting at a different eligible site, she said.
The group wants to help people prepare, Turner-Osborne said. “But I don’t want it to be in a way that deters people from voting.”
IT’S EVEN WORSE THAN WE THOUGHT.
What we’re seeing right now from Donald Trump is a full-on authoritarian takeover of the U.S. government.
This is not hyperbole.
Court orders are being ignored. MAGA loyalists have been put in charge of the military and federal law enforcement agencies. The Department of Government Efficiency has stripped Congress of its power of the purse. News outlets that challenge Trump have been banished or put under investigation.
Yet far too many are still covering Trump’s assault on democracy like politics as usual, with flattering headlines describing Trump as “unconventional,” “testing the boundaries,” and “aggressively flexing power.”
The Intercept has long covered authoritarian governments, billionaire oligarchs, and backsliding democracies around the world. We understand the challenge we face in Trump and the vital importance of press freedom in defending democracy.
We’re independent of corporate interests. Will you help us?
IT’S BEEN A DEVASTATING year for journalism — the worst in modern U.S. history.
We have a president with utter contempt for truth aggressively using the government’s full powers to dismantle the free press. Corporate news outlets have cowered, becoming accessories in Trump’s project to create a post-truth America. Right-wing billionaires have pounced, buying up media organizations and rebuilding the information environment to their liking.
In this most perilous moment for democracy, The Intercept is fighting back. But to do so effectively, we need to grow.
That’s where you come in. Will you help us expand our reporting capacity in time to hit the ground running in 2026?
We’re independent of corporate interests. Will you help us?

lemonde.fr/en.title: Evacuated Ukrainians from Oleshky: 'We don't know where to go, but one thing is certain: We will survive'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Some burst into tears, while others looked dazed and struggled to grasp that they had escaped hell. Many seemed stunned to find themselves in Ukraine, surrounded by the calming atmosphere of a forest on the Belarusian border. They rushed for what they had missed the most: cigarettes and hot soup.
Leaving Oleshky during a six-day local ceasefire negotiated between Kyiv and Moscow, transported by bus to Russian-occupied Crimea and then by plane to Belarus, those who chose to come to Ukraine arrived on Saturday, October 31, in a state of utter exhaustion, caught between relief and shock, after years of war and occupation and months of famine, without water, electricity or medical aid.
The evacuees from Oleshky, a city in southern Ukraine located across the Dnipro River from Kherson, had lived under Russian occupation since Moscow's army seized the region on the first day of the war, February 24, 2022. After Ukrainian forces liberated Kherson on November 11, 2022, the Russian army retreated to the southern side of the Dnipro. Oleshky then became the frontline city on the Russian side, just as Kherson was on the Ukrainian side.
Then, over four years, as drone warfare escalated and the frontline was gradually abandoned, the Russian army slowly pulled its positions back from the Dnipro, maintaining control of the area but leaving Oleshky behind. The city effectively ended up on the frontline, in a no man's land, right in the middle of what military personnel now call the "Kill Zone," an area of death where nothing survives.
The hell of living in a 'frontline city'

lemonde.fr/en.title: French high schoolers return from break with protest turnout uncertain but vows to 'keep up pressure'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
French schools closed their doors for the fall break on Friday, October 16, right in the middle of a youth movement of a scale not seen in decades, one that showed no sign of losing steam. They reopened on Monday, November 2, amid uncertainty: Would classes resume only to be met with renewed blockades at the high schools this very morning? Everyone – in high schoolers' social media groups, in ministry offices or in school leadership – wondered what would become of the movement and are waiting to see how calls to protest from university and high school students will play out on the ground. As of Monday morning, 41 establishments, amounting to 1% of the country's high schools, were closed, according to the Education Ministry.
There were many unknowns as classes returned. For high schoolers, the autumn break lasted two weeks; but for the movement they launched in mid-September, it feels like a century has passed. On October 17, the mobilization widened significantly, joined by a movement "against the high cost of living" and in defense of public services, which brought together hundreds of thousands of demonstrators across France, who gathered on the following Saturdays, October 24 and 31.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Post-Orban Hungary faces challenge of rebuilding public trust
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Six months into its tenure, with Prime Minister Péter Magyar's government still far from settled in, representatives of civil society in Hungary say they finally feel they can breathe again after 16 years under Viktor Orban's regime. Still, they remain "cautiously optimistic," as Aron Demeter, communications manager for the Hungarian branch of human rights non-governmental organization Amnesty International, put it.
"The atmosphere we are working in now is completely different; we are free from the heavy burden of being portrayed as 'enemies of Hungary,'" said Demeter, who has spent 13 years with the NGO. Under Orban, who suffered a resounding defeat in the April 2026 elections, NGOs faced relentless smear campaigns and laws that complicated their work, even if did not make it outright impossible.
This was especially true for organizations defending human rights and minority rights (including those of the Roma in Hungary), most of which received funding from abroad. As a result, the authorities accused them of being "foreign agents" and "puppets" of philanthropist George Soros, who is of Hungarian descent.

lemonde.fr/en.title: France expels five Britons arrested for harrassing migrants
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Five Britons arrested in France on suspicion of harassing migrants were on Sunday, November 2, fined, expelled and banned from entering the region for six months, French authorities said. The five, from an "ultra-right movement," were arrested on Thursday while broadcasting live footage online near the northern Channel port of Dunkirk, said the local prefecture.
An aid group had accused them of violence against undocumented migrants, but investigations failed to establish evidence of violent offenses, prosecutor Charlotte Huet said in a statement Sunday. The five men, aged between 30 and 46, were found carrying tear gas and pepper spray canisters, as well as a stick and a baton, which are illegal to carry under French law. A judge banned them from the Nord and Pas-de-Calais departments for six months and ordered them to pay €500 each to a victims' support association.
"All five were expelled from French territory on Sunday," an official in the Hauts-de-France and Nord regional prefecture told AFP.
In January, two Britons suspected of having come to France to take part in a banned anti-migrant action in the Channel port of Calais were arrested and deported. Ten other British far-right activists had been banned from French territory in mid-January after being accused of violence in previous months against migrants on the French coast.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Bulgarian president wins runoff vote as Black Sea attacks raise stakes
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Bulgaria's President Iliana Yotova, who favors dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, won a presidential runoff vote on Sunday, November 2. The race for the largely ceremonial post had pitted Yotova, an ally of Prime Minister Rumen Radev, against Andrey Gyurov, a banker and former caretaker prime minister backed by the pro-Western opposition.
Yotova gained between 57.4% and 58.2% of the vote, according to estimates from several polling institutes, well ahead of Gyurov, who garnered between 38.6% and 39.6%. Flanked by Radev, a jubilant Yotova declared victory, saying her message had focused on "incomes, peace and the challenges that lie ahead."
EU chief Ursula von der Leyen congratulated Yotova.
"From security and defence to our competitiveness and energy independence, I look forward to continuing our joint work. For a strong Bulgaria in a strong Europe," she said on X.
'Clear path forward'
The election was held against a backdrop of a series of drone attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea that have raised security concerns. Several vessels were struck in the Black Sea off Bulgaria in October, leaving 21 people missing, in what is thought to be spillover from the Russia-Ukraine war. While center-left Radev has said the attacks appeared to serve Russian interests and summoned the Russian ambassador, his government insists there is so far no evidence directly linking them to Moscow.
"Today, the Bulgarian people have chosen the future over the past," said Radev, who also advocates dialogue with Moscow. "They have opted for normalcy and a stable, clear path forward."
Yotova, 62, took over the post of president earlier this year from Radev, who stepped down to run in parliamentary elections. Sunday's vote means she is set to become the first elected woman president in the country of 6.4 million people.
Gyurov, 50 and a former deputy governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, told reporters that he accepted "the results as they are. "We have laid a solid foundation upon which we can build," he added, emphasizing the importance of seeking unity.
Historically close to Russia, Bulgaria remains deeply divided over its relationship with Moscow. After voting in Sofia, Yotova said she wanted "Bulgaria to be strong in a strong Europe" and remain "sovereign in its decisions."
A longtime ally of Radev, she supports Bulgaria's EU and NATO membership while arguing that peace in Ukraine can be achieved only through negotiations. A former journalist and member of the European Parliament, Yotova was elected vice president alongside Radev in 2016 and 2021.
Gyurov said after voting that he had voted for a "secure, stable and European Bulgaria." The first round, where Yotova narrowly won over Gyurov, recorded a record low turnout of 23%. Turnout in the second round was projected to be around 27%.

lemonde.fr/en.title: US midterms: In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed's Democratic rival backs Republican Senate candidate in stunning move
lemonde.fr/en.text:
The Senate race in Michigan is already one of the most closely watched in the country, and just two days before the vote on Tuesday, November 3, it took an unexpected turn. Haley Stevens, a Democratic member of Congress who lost her party's primary to Abdul El-Sayed in August, publicly endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers on Sunday. This reversal could have a major impact on this tight race, the outcome of which is critical for control of the Senate.
Stevens released a video filmed in her car to announce her support for the opposing camp. "Hey Michigan, as you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for US Senate, Abdul, said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away. And he's right, and that's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the United States Senate today. I don't belong in Abdul's campaign." Earlier, she joined the Republican candidate at a religious service at Detroit's Perfecting Church, a Black community church in the city.
This blow to the Democratic campaign capped months of mounting tension. The primary was extremely contentious between the two candidates, particularly over the situation in the Middle East. El-Sayed, 42, who would become the first Muslim to serve in the Senate if victorious on Tuesday, is staunchly pro-Palestinian, while Stevens, 43, is one of Israel's strongest supporters among Democrats in Congress. Pro-Israel advocacy groups in the US poured nearly $40 million into supporting Stevens's candidacy – or attacking El-Sayed's. It was to no avail.

lemonde.fr/en.title: 'I might let my children vote for me': Inside the minds of France's undecided voters
lemonde.fr/en.text:
They are known as swing voters, the undecided, sometimes even the fickle. They are the voters who make pollsters' predictions uncertain, the ones candidates work tirelessly to persuade in hopes of picking up a few extra votes. Some reject Marine Le Pen's political views, yet feel tempted to vote for her far-right Rassemblement National (RN) party to "turn the system upside down." Others wonder whether to "vote with their head or with their heart." Some have always been on the left but strongly oppose radical-left Jean-Luc Mélenchon's candidacy and fear him advancing to the 2nd round of the presidential election. Some even contemplate, after 54 years of never missing a vote, staying home on April 18, 2027, the first round of the election, to avoid "signing a blank check" to candidates they consider "unworthy."
With less than six months to go before the first round of France's presidential election, undecided voters interviewed by Le Monde described the difficulty of breaking with party loyalties and the anxiety of having to choose from a slate of candidates who are either too far from their own beliefs or divided among too many competing contenders. Will they vote at all? If they vote, will it be out of conviction or calculation? And for which candidate?

lemonde.fr/en.title: Tens of thousands protest in India's capital against voter roll revision
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Tens of thousands joined a protest led by opposition politicians in India's capital on Sunday, November 1, renewing demands for the country's election chief to resign over an overhaul of voter lists they say unfairly benefits the ruling party. The nationwide revision of electoral rolls has sparked political disputes and street protests in the world's largest democracy over the last month.
The Election Commission says the initiative is necessary to ensure accurate voter lists, but the opposition claims it is being manipulated to favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Both the BJP and the Election Commission deny the allegations.
On Sunday, protesters led by opposition Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi chanted "vote thief, leave your seat" and beat drums while marching from central parts of New Delhi to Ramlila Maidan, a large outdoor venue.
'Theft of the voice'
Gandhi, who traveled to the venue in an open-top jeep, said protesters were "not prepared to accept" the voter list removals. "It is the theft of the voice of every single citizen of India," he said during a speech. "This protest does not belong to any political party. It is India's protest to save the democracy and constitution."
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online youth-led protest movement, has also thrown its weight behind the opposition campaign. The overhaul of India's voter rolls has resulted in more than 133 million names being removed from electoral lists, according to figures reported by Indian media and cited by opposition parties in court filings.
Undocumented migrants
Members of the BJP have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighboring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India's electoral rolls. Election authorities say the revision was intended to eliminate duplicate, deceased and fraudulent entries, and that eligible voters remain entitled to apply for inclusion on the roll.
The Cockroach movement has been heavily involved in the pushback to the voter-roll revision and several of its leaders were temporarily detained by police during protests last month.
The CJP has gained millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May. Earlier protests organized by the CJP in July over exam irregularities forced the resignation of the education minister, marking a rare climbdown by Modi's administration.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Nine killed in jet crash in Palm Beach, Florida
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Nine people were killed Sunday when the Learjet they were traveling in plummeted into a neighborhood in southern Florida, officials said. Several unverified clips depicting the deadly crash and posted to social media show an aircraft nearly vertical slamming at high speed into the ground and triggering a large fireball, leaving a flaming crater near a busy roadside.
"Today's plane crash in Palm Beach County, Florida is a horrific tragedy," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement, confirming that all nine people on board were killed.
Duffy said the plane, a Learjet 60, had departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed for the Bahamas. The crash occurred near Cresthaven, a neighborhood in Palm Beach County that is less than 7 miles (11 kilometers) from Mar-a-Lago.
Trump himself had been at Mar-a-Lago on Sunday and had departed from the nearby and newly renamed President Donald J Trump International Airport shortly after he boarded Air Force One at 11:55 am, about an hour before the crash of the Learjet aircraft.
Storms had been reported in the area.
"The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate" the crash, the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Why the 'elite overproduction' theory is misunderstanding young people's anger
lemonde.fr/en.text:
High school and university students flooding the streets? The bust of Marianne shattered on the floor of the Marseille city hall? The wave of youthful "Mélenchonmania"? Look no further: All of that is said to be the result of an "overproduction of elites." The phrase has become fashionable in conservative circles. France is allegedly producing too many university graduates for the number of high-level positions available, which would explain the frustration and anger of a generation aspiring to elevated status.
The "radicalism" of young French people, including those from privileged families, stems from this mismatch. As a result, 42% of 18- to 24-year-olds were planning to vote for radical-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon in the 2027 presidential election (compared to 21% for far-right candidate Marine Le Pen and 4% for center-left candidate Raphaël Glucksmann), according to an Ipsos BVA-CESI Ecole d'ingénieurs survey conducted from September 3 to 9 for Le Monde, Sciences Po, the Fondation Jean Jaurès and the Institut Montaigne. In 2022, 31% already voted for Mélenchon, and the figure rose to 34% among 25- to 34-year-olds.

lemonde.fr/en.title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after Molotov cocktail attack on riot police
lemonde.fr/en.text:
France on Sunday, November 1, launched an attempted murder probe after a petrol bomb were thrown at security forces during Paris protests.
On Saturday, clashes erupted in Paris and other cities after hundreds of thousands of people peacefully demonstrated against soaring living costs, police violence and racism.
The Paris police prefecture said that several hundred rioters had attacked security forces with projectiles, including a Molotov cocktail. While riots were less widespread than two weeks ago, when France experienced some of its worst unrest in years, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Saturday that the level of violence perpetrated by some was "extraordinary." Dramatic images, showed a homemade incendiary device exploding at the feet of a security officer in protective gear, engulfing his lower body in flames.
Prosecutors that said an investigation had been opened for "attempted murder of persons vested with public authority." "Explosive devices were thrown at around 15 gendarmes as well as police officers," the prosecutor's office said.
An assessment of the injured was ongoing, prosecutors said, adding that the reported injuries included second-degree burns.
The officer struck by the Molotov cocktail said his unit was "under assault," with glass bottles, paving stones, shards of glass and firebombs thrown at them. "We were hit by several significant incendiary devices," he told broadcaster RTL on condition of anonymity. "The flammable substance was so greasy that I could feel it spreading across my skin," he said. "I kept wondering when it would stop because I really felt as though I had been coated by the heat itself."
The officer, who received minor injuries, said the leg and shin protections on his riot uniform melted. After watching the footage of the firebomb attack that injured him, he said he was surprised by "the intensity" of the incident. The video made him realize "that we may also have come close to a catastrophe." His unit had been on leave but was recalled ahead of the protests. The gendarmerie said that 13 members of the officer's unit were injured, according to RTL.
No suspects "have been arrested at this stage in connection with the incident," the prosecutor's office said, adding that investigators were working to identify those responsible.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Biodiversity COP17: Leading negotiator Steven Guilbeault believes harmful subsidies will be 'main battleground in the coming years'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
After two weeks of negotiations and a final night of heated debate, the 17th Conference of the Parties on Biodiversity (COP17) ended in Yerevan, Armenia, on Saturday morning, October 31. Steven Guilbeault, former Canadian environment minister and key architect of the 2022 Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, analyzed how far this COP will help achieve the 23 targets set to save biodiversity by 2030.
COP17 was supposed to assess global progress since 2022 and renew momentum toward the 2030 biodiversity targets. Do you think it lived up to expectations?
Yes, absolutely. I think the Armenian presidency did an exemplary job. First, the review, conducted four years after the Kunming-Montreal Framework, gave us an accurate picture of what is working and what is not. Second, they offered us a clear roadmap for the way ahead.
Critics feel that the first text adopted last night, the 'Yerevan Pathway,' is too cautious in its language and lacks ambition.
I do not share that view. Of course, the presidency cannot go further than what all member countries allow, it is a consensus-driven process. But the Yerevan Pathway clearly shows the presidency's intent to put the issue of harmful subsidies front and center, which will likely be the main battleground in the coming years.

lemonde.fr/en.title: The debate over a factoryless French industry is making a comeback
lemonde.fr/en.text:
The remark did not go unnoticed. "We are not going to reopen factories, that's a myth!" declared Jean Tirole, the 2014 Nobel laureate in economics, on French television on September 10. According to the economist, who argued that trying to rebuild a traditional industrial base was a doomed effort in a global economic war dominated by two superpowers – China and the US – France must stop "focusing on reindustrialization." He regretted that, like Europe, France "continues to invest in yesterday's industry," when, in his view, all efforts should be put into breakthrough technologies such as artificial intelligence or biotechnology to compete with the new US and Chinese empires.
The economist's comments came as France's push for industrial recovery, launched in the wake of the Covid-19 crisis, which exposed the critical issues of dependence and sovereignty, has struggled to gain traction. While some industries have taken advantage of the international context to grow, such as defense and low-carbon energy, many traditional manufacturing sectors (including steel, automotive, plastics and glass) have faced crises and called for government subsidies and protective measures to withstand falling demand in Europe as well as competition from the so-called "Chinese shock." Illustrating France's difficulties, the share of industry in national gross domestic product (GDP) has not increased in six years, remaining stuck at 10%, compared with 18% in Germany and 16% in Italy.

welt.de.title: Trump-Regierung drängt plötzlich auf russische Gaslieferungen für Europa
welt.de.text: Washington drängt nach Informationen des „Wall Street Journal“ auf eine rasche Wiederaufnahme russischer Erdgaslieferungen nach Europa über die Ukraine. Der Vorschlag soll dem Bericht zufolge Teil der Bemühungen um eine Waffenruhe bei Angriffen auf die Energieinfrastruktur Russlands und der Ukraine vor dem kommenden Winter sein. Die US-Unterhändler Jared Kushner und Steve Witkoff hätten die Idee demnach bereits im September bei Gesprächen in Moskau und Kiew vorgebracht,  schreibt das Blatt. (verlinkt auf https://www.wsj.com/world/europe/u-s-pushes-to-restore-russian-gas-sales-to-europe-via-ukraine-0ca62dc7?mod=hp_lead_pos1) Vorgesehen sei, russisches Gas durch das bestehende Pipeline-Netz über die Ukraine nach Europa zu leiten. Dabei könnte ein US-amerikanischer Vermittler eingeschaltet werden. Einnahmen Russlands aus den Lieferungen könnten nach Vorstellungen des Weißen Hauses dann wiederum auf einem Treuhandkonto in einem Drittstaat hinterlegt werden, um zu verhindern, dass Moskau das Geld unmittelbar zur Finanzierung des Krieges verwendet. Die Ukraine wiederum könnte Transitgebühren einnehmen. Washington erhofft sich von dem Modell zugleich einen Anreiz für Kremlchef Wladimir Putin, einer umfassenden Waffenruhe im Energiebereich zuzustimmen. Neue Dringlichkeit hätten die Bemühungen vor geplanten Verhandlungen der USA, Russlands und der Ukraine Mitte November in Abu Dhabi erhalten, heißt es. „Ich würde Russland ganz sicher nicht vertrauen“, so EU-Energiekommissar Dan Jørgensen In Europa dürfte der Vorschlag allerdings auf erheblichen Widerstand stoßen. EU-Energiekommissar Dan Jørgensen hatte erst im Oktober deutlich gemacht, dass er auch im Falle eines Friedensschlusses an einem dauerhaften Importstopp festhalten will. „Ich würde Russland ganz sicher nicht vertrauen“, sagte Jørgensen. Die EU hat beschlossen, russische Gasimporte bis Ende 2027 auslaufen zu lassen. Vor dem russischen Angriff auf die Ukraine kamen dem Bericht zufolge noch 45 Prozent des europäischen Erdgases aus Russland, inzwischen seien es nur noch elf Prozent. US-Flüssiggas decke dagegen rund 30 Prozent des europäischen Verbrauchs. Europäische Regierungsvertreter betonen bislang, eine erneute Abhängigkeit von russischer Energie komme auch nach einem möglichen Friedensschluss nicht infrage. Bemerkenswert ist der Kurswechsel Washingtons auch mit Blick auf die frühere Bundeskanzlerin Angela Merkel. In Trumps erster Amtszeit hatte der US-Präsident Merkel wegen des Baus von Nord Stream 2 wiederholt scharf kritisiert und Deutschland vorgeworfen, sich damit zum „Gefangenen Russlands“ zu machen. Ende 2019 verhängten die USA sogar Sanktionen gegen das Pipelineprojekt. Nun vertritt die Trump-Regierung nach Darstellung des „Wall Street Journal“ eine deutlich andere Linie: Ein hochrangiger US-Regierungsvertreter bezeichnete es dem Bericht zufolge als Merkels Fehler, Nord Stream vorangetrieben zu haben, ohne zuvor eine umfassendere Sicherheitsvereinbarung mit Russland anzustreben. Washington betrachtet eine Wiederbelebung russischer Gaslieferungen inzwischen offenbar als möglichen Bestandteil einer größeren Vereinbarung mit Moskau.

welt.de.title: Eklat erschüttert US-Wahlkampf – Demokraten werfen eigener Politikerin „verachtenswerten Verrat“ vor
welt.de.text: Kurz vor den US-Kongresswahlen werden die oppositionellen Demokraten im wichtigen Bundesstaat Michigan von internen Kämpfen erschüttert. Die demokratische Abgeordnete Haley Stevens, die ihrem linksgerichteten Parteikollegen Abdul El-Sayed in einer Senats-Vorwahl unterlegen war, stellte sich am Sonntag hinter den Senatskandidaten der Republikaner von Präsident Donald Trump. „Wir alle wissen, dass das eine sehr enge Wahl ist“, sagte Stevens zu Journalisten. „Aber Abdul hat sehr deutlich gemacht, dass ich in seinem Wahlkampf nicht willkommen bin.“ Die Abgeordnete sprach stattdessen dem republikanischen Senatskandidaten Mike Rogers ihre Unterstützung aus. El-Sayed zeigte sich unbeeindruckt von der Entscheidung der abtrünnigen Parteikollegin. „Letztlich denke ich nicht an Haley Stevens“, sagte er vor Journalisten. „Ich denke an die 9,999998 Millionen Menschen, die nicht die beiden sind“, fügte er mit Blick auf Stevens und Rogers hinzu. Der Minderheitsführer der Demokraten im US-Senat, Chuck Schumer, fand härtere Worte für Stevens: Er warf ihr einen „verachtenswerten Verrat“ vor. Trump, der El-Sayed als „Dschihadisten“ beschimpft hat, sagte dagegen, Stevens habe „Mut“. US-Präsident Donald Trump lobte Stevens nach ihrer Wahlempfehlung für Rogers. Stevens habe Mut und große, nahezu beispiellose Loyalität gegenüber den Menschen in Michigan bewiesen, schrieb Trump auf seiner Plattform Truth Social. Wenn El-Sayed gewinnt, wäre der frühere Chef des Gesundheitsamts von Detroit der erste muslimische US-Senator. Der Ex-FBI-Agent Rogers vertrat Michigan bereits bis 2015 im US-Repräsentantenhaus und will nun den Fokus unter anderem auf die nationale Sicherheit legen. Der Senat gilt als besonders umkämpft Hunderte Abgeordnete, 35 Senatoren und zahlreiche Gouverneure werden bei den US-Zwischenwahlen am Dienstag neu bestimmt. Doch wie der Abend für die Republikaner und die oppositionellen Demokraten ausgeht, entscheidet sich voraussichtlich in einer deutlich kleineren Zahl besonders umkämpfter Rennen. Im Senat haben die Republikaner derzeit 53 der insgesamt 100 Sitze. Die Demokraten halten 45 Sitze und können sich auf die Unterstützung von zwei Parteilosen verlassen. Bei den Midterms werden 35 Sitze neu vergeben. Würden die Demokraten den Republikanern netto vier Sitze abnehmen, hätte Trumps Partei keine Mehrheit mehr. Laut Wahlanalytikern der Plattform „Cook Political Report“ zeichnet sich bei sieben Sitzen ein Kopf-an-Kopf-Rennen ab – die Mehrheit davon ist aktuell republikanisch besetzt. Das sind neben Michigan die wichtigsten Senatswahlen: Texas:  Der Bundesstaat galt in den vergangenen Jahrzehnten als republikanische Hochburg. Entsprechend verheerend wäre es für Trumps Partei, wenn sie dort einen Senatssitz verlieren würde. Für die Demokraten wäre es dagegen ihr erster Sieg bei einem Senatsrennen in dem südlichen Bundesstaat seit fast 40 Jahren. Ihr Kandidat, der frühere Lehrer James Talarico, tritt gegen den republikanischen Generalstaatsanwalt Ken Paxton an. Dieser gilt als Unterstützer Trumps und ist umstritten. So musste er sich etwa einem Amtsenthebungsverfahren wegen Vorwürfen von Korruption und Amtsmissbrauch stellen. Talarico stellte sich im Wahlkampf als Politiker dar, der in Washington für ein bezahlbares Leben kämpfen will. Immer wieder machte er auch seinen christlichen Glauben zum Thema. Alaska:  Wird eine Namensgleichheit dem republikanischen Amtsinhaber Dan S. Sullivan Stimmen kosten – und damit seinen Senatssitz? Diese Sorge hat zumindest die Trump-Regierung geschürt. Gegen den Amtsinhaber treten der politische Neuling Dan J. Sullivan und die Demokratin Mary Peltola an. Republikaner verdächtigen die Demokraten schon länger, den Namensvetter aus taktischem Kalkül zur Kandidatur bewogen zu haben und auf eine Verwechslungsgefahr zu setzen. Ein Medienbericht hat ihre Darstellung jüngst untermauert. Das Rennen war zeitweise Gegenstand einer juristischen Auseinandersetzung, in die auch das US-Justizministerium involviert ist. Mittlerweile wurde die Klage abgewiesen. Gouverneure nicht ignorieren: Chefs der Bundesstaaten Zwar nehmen sie auf Bundesebene eine vergleichsweise kleinere Rolle ein – in ihren Bundesstaaten haben die Gouverneurinnen und Gouverneure allerdings das mächtigste Amt. Sollten die Demokraten mindestens zwei zusätzliche Gouverneure stellen, gäbe es erstmals seit 2010 wieder mehr demokratische als republikanische Bundesstaatenchefs. Im Fokus stehen etwa: Ohio:  Mit einem umstrittenen Werbevideo hatte der republikanische Unternehmer Vivek Ramaswamy Stimmung gegen seine demokratische Kontrahentin Amy Acton gemacht. In dem Video rief die Mutter der Ärztin die Wähler auf, nicht für ihre Tochter zu stimmen – obwohl beide seit Jahren keinen Kontakt mehr zueinander haben. Acton hatte den Kontakt zu ihrer Mutter abgebrochen, nachdem sie nach eigenen Angaben sexuell von ihrem Stiefvater missbraucht worden war. Ramaswamys Kampagne hatte parteiübergreifend für Kritik gesorgt – selbst der scheidende republikanische Amtsinhaber äußerte Unmut. Wisconsin:  In dem Bundesstaat entscheidet sich, ob sich der moderate Demokrat David Crowley gegen den Republikaner Tom Tiffany durchsetzen kann. Der Swing State wurde zuletzt demokratisch regiert, doch in der Vergangenheit entschieden bei Präsidentschafts- und Gouverneurswahlen oft nur wenige Tausend Stimmen. Crowley hatte sich parteiintern mit einem gemäßigteren Ansatz etwa beim Reizthema Gesundheitsvorsorge gegen die linke Kandidatin Francesca Hong durchgesetzt. Falls er den Ex-Kongressabgeordneten Tiffany schlägt, könnte das als positives Signal für moderate Kandidaten der Demokraten gewertet werden. Gute Chancen für die Demokraten Umfragen bescheinigen Demokraten gute Chancen, das Repräsentantenhaus zu gewinnen. Aktuell ist die Mehrheit der Republikaner dort äußerst knapp: 218 der 435 Sitze sind in republikanischer Hand, die Demokraten haben 214. Die anderen drei sind entweder vakant oder von einem Parteilosen besetzt. Zwar stehen alle Sitze zur Wahl. Da eine ganze Reihe an Sitzen feste Hochburgen der einen oder anderen Partei sind, stehen aber auch hier vor allem die umkämpften Wahlkreise im Fokus: Gewinnt eine Partei hier überproportional viel, deutet das früh auf einen Gesamtsieg hin.

welt.de.title: „Man konnte die Irritation in Xis Gesicht feststellen“, sagt Steinmeier
welt.de.text: China zeigt nach Darstellung von Bundespräsident Frank-Walter Steinmeier kein Interesse an einem Dreiergipfel mit Russland und den USA zur  Ukraine (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article6ae826135e7018b4bea95568/ukraine-krieg-wenn-ihr-wollt-selenskyj-knuepft-angriffsstopp-fuer-raffinerien-an-bedingungen.html) . Er habe den chinesischen Präsidenten Xi Jinping bei ihrem Treffen in Peking darauf angesprochen, sagte  Steinmeier (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/deutschland/plus6ae0c5edf74d161423be05f8/bundespraesident-gesucht-der-naechste-praesident-muss-der-sprachstoerung-zwischen-regierenden-und-regierten-entgegenwirken.html)  im „Bericht aus Berlin“ der ARD. Nach dessen Antwort werde es wohl beim bevorstehenden Apec-Gipfel in Shenzhen tatsächlich ein Treffen der Präsidenten der drei Staaten geben. Hierbei solle es aber nicht um die Ukraine gehen. Er habe Xi direkt auf Berichte über einen möglichen Dreiergipfel angesprochen. „Und man konnte die Irritation in seinem Gesicht feststellen, weil er anschließend auch gefragt hat, woher solche Gerüchte kommen“, sagte Steinmeier, der sich am Freitag mit Xi in Peking getroffen hatte. Inzwischen ist er in Berlin zurück. „Es ist nach seiner Auffassung keinerlei Vorbereitung für einen Ukraine-Gipfel unter Beteiligung der USA, Russlands und Chinas am Horizont“, berichtete Steinmeier aus seinem Gespräch mit Xi. „Er hat ausdrücklich darauf hingewiesen, dass dies ein europäischer Konflikt sei, bei dem die Europäer mit am Tisch sitzen müssten.“ Hintergrund sind Berichte über einen möglichen Dreiergipfel am Rande der Konferenz der Asiatisch-Pazifischen Wirtschaftsgemeinschaft (Apec) Mitte November. Russlands Präsident Wladimir Putin hatte ein solches Treffen vorgeschlagen, um über Fragen der nuklearen Abrüstung zu reden. US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte sich dafür offen gezeigt und erklärt, er würde bei einer solchen Gelegenheit auch weitere Themen „wie die Ukraine“ ansprechen.

welt.de.title: „Wenn ihr wollt …“ – Selenskyj knüpft Angriffsstopp für Raffinerien an Bedingungen
welt.de.text: Der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj hat den Stopp ukrainischer Angriffe auf russische Ölanlagen gegenüber den USA an Bedingungen geknüpft. „Wenn ihr wollt, dass wir keine russischen Raffinerien mehr angreifen, dann darf Russland auch unser Energiesystem nicht mehr angreifen“, sagte Selenskyj am Sonntag dem US-Sender  Fox News (verlinkt auf https://www.foxnews.com/video/6407755033112) . „Eine andere Möglichkeit wäre: Gebt uns Patriot-Raketen.“ Selenskyj äußerte sich gegenüber dem US-Sender, nachdem er nach eigenen Angaben „mehrere verschiedene“ Gespräche mit US-Präsident Donald Trump und dessen Stab zu diesem Thema geführt habe. „Wir haben klargestellt, dass wir nicht untätig bleiben können, nachdem Russland unsere Energieinfrastruktur angegriffen, unsere Menschen getötet und unsere Strom- und Gasversorgung sowie unsere Raffinerien – kurz: alles – attackiert hat“, sagte der ukrainische Staatschef in dem Interview. Hinsichtlich seiner Forderung zur Lieferung von Luftabwehrraketen vom Typ Patriot fügte Selenskyj hinzu: „Die Finanzierung dafür werden wir sicherstellen, es geht nicht nur um Hilfsgelder.“ Konkret bot Selenskyj der US-Regierung demnach an, dass Kiew die Angriffe auf russische Raffinerien für einen Monat aussetzen würde, falls Washington für diesen Zeitraum die entsprechenden Raketensysteme bereitstelle. Die Frage, ob er befürchte, dies könne als Versuch ausgelegt werden, Trump unter Druck zu setzen, verneinte Selenskyj. „Ich habe keinerlei Bedenken, wenn ich unter Partnern die Wahrheit ausspreche“, sagte er. Zuletzt hatte die US-Regierung am Freitag den Verkauf von 500 Patriot-Abfangraketen an die Ukraine genehmigt. Bis die Waffen tatsächlich dort eintreffen, könnten aber noch Jahre vergehen. Selenskyj hatte die Entscheidung zwar begrüßt, forderte angesichts der langen Lieferzeit aber eine Übergangslösung. Er schlug vor, dass die USA und europäische Verbündete zunächst Raketen aus ihren Beständen an die Ukraine abgeben und diese später durch die neu bestellten Waffen ersetzen. Seit Trumps Amtsantritt Anfang 2025 haben die USA ihre direkten Militärhilfen für die Ukraine eingestellt. Über den sogenannten Purl-Mechanismus können Verbündete jedoch Waffenpakete in den USA für Kiew kaufen. Deutschland beteiligte sich bereits an drei solchen Paketen und sagte im Juni weitere 200 Millionen Dollar (180 Millionen Euro) für ein Waffenpaket sowie zusätzlich 200 Millionen Dollar für Patriot-Abfangraketen zu. Zuletzt hatte Selenskyj den USA allerdings vorgeworfen, die Lieferung von Raketen im Rahmen des Purl-Programms zu verzögern. Trump hatte Kiew scharf für die Angriffe auf russische Ölanlagen kritisiert, weil er sie für die steigenden Energiepreise verantwortlich macht. Zuletzt hatten sich Washington und Moskau auf ein Dieselabkommen geeinigt, das in der Ukraine Empörung hervorrief. Das von Trump vereinbarte Geschäft war durch Lockerungen der US-Sanktionen ermöglicht worden. Die Ukraine und ihre europäischen Verbündeten hatten es kritisiert. Selenskyj zu Treffen mit Putin in der Türkei bereit In einem weiteren Interview erklärte sich der ukrainische Präsident zu einem direkten Treffen mit Kremlchef Wladimir Putin in der Türkei bereit. Nach seinen Worten sei auch über die Möglichkeit eines Treffens auf der Ebene der Staats- und Regierungschefs im Dreierformat gesprochen worden, sagte Selenskyj im Sender CNN Türk. Wenn die Türkei dies ermöglichen könne, würde die Ukraine es akzeptieren und sich darüber freuen. Später im Interview sagt er auf die Frage, ob er bereit sei, Putin in der Türkei zu treffen: „Ja, wir sind zu einem solchen Treffen bereit.“ Selenskyj hat bereits mehrfach seine Bereitschaft zu einem direkten Treffen mit Putin bekundet. Putin hatte wiederum stets angeboten, sich mit Selenskyj in Moskau zu treffen. Dies jedoch lehnt der ukrainische Staatschef kategorisch ab. App für Notfall-Warnungen in Ukraine und Russland gehackt In der Ukraine und in Russland sind die offiziellen Notfall-Apps nach Behördenangaben gehackt worden. Zunächst wurde am späten Sonntagabend in der ukrainischen App unter anderem fälschlicherweise vor radioaktiver Strahlung in der Hauptstadt Kiew gewarnt. Die App „Air Alert“ sei möglicherweise vom Feind kompromittiert worden, teilte die ukrainische Luftwaffe auf Telegram mit. Es bestehe keine Gefahr durch Strahlung. In der Nacht zum Montag meldete dann Russland einen massiven Cyberangriff auf seine Warn-App, wie die staatliche Nachrichtenagentur Tass unter Berufung auf das Zivilschutzministerium berichtete. Es sei den Angreifern gelungen, Falschinformationen an die Bevölkerung zu versenden, hieß es weiter. Die russische Behörde machte keine Angaben dazu, wen sie hinter dem Angriff vermutete. Die Webseite des Ministeriums für Warnungen war in der Nacht zeitweise nicht erreichbar. War es ein ukrainischer Gegenangriff auf das russische System? Die zeitliche Abfolge der Ereignisse lässt die Vermutung zu, dass es sich nach der Attacke auf das ukrainische System um einen Gegenangriff Kiews gehandelt haben könnte. Russland greift das kleinere Nachbarland Ukraine seit viereinhalb Jahren massiv aus der Luft, am Boden und auf hoher See an. Es kommt dabei auch zu Cyberangriffen, die allerdings deutlich seltener Schlagzeilen machen. Luftangriffe – und die nötigen regionalen Warnungen davor – sind für die Menschen in der Ukraine längst Alltag. Bei größeren Angriffen auf Kiew suchen Menschen häufig in den Stationen der U-Bahn Schutz.

welt.de.title: Russlandfreundliche Amtsinhaberin Jotowa klare Siegerin bei Präsidentschaftswahl
welt.de.text: Richtungsentscheidung bei der Präsidentschaftswahl in Bulgarien: Die russlandfreundliche  Amtsinhaberin Ilijana Jotowa (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article6ae782745e7018b4bea95076/stichwahl-russlandfreundliche-praesidentin-jotowa-liegt-nach-prognosen-in-bulgarien-vorn.html)  hat die Stichwahl in dem EU- und Nato-Mitgliedsland am Sonntag klar für sich entschieden. Laut Prognosen setzte sich die Staatschefin mit deutlichem Vorsprung gegen ihren pro-westlichen Herausforderer Andrej Gjurow durch. Dieser räumte noch am Wahlabend seine Niederlage ein. EU-Kommissionspräsidentin Ursula von der Leyen gratulierte Jotowa zu ihrem Wahlsieg. Jotowa, die sich für einen Dialog mit Moskau und gegen Militärhilfen für die Ukraine ausspricht, erreichte den jüngsten Prognosen zufolge zwischen 57,4 und 58,2 Prozent der Stimmen. Auf Gjurow entfielen demnach zwischen 38,6 und 39,6 Prozent. Mit ihrem Sieg in der Stichwahl wird Jotowa die erste Frau als gewähltes Staatsoberhaupt – die Nachfolge ihres Vorgängers Rumen Radew hatte sie ohne Wahl angetreten. Der Urnengang galt vor allem als Entscheidung über den außenpolitischen Kurs Bulgariens, insbesondere mit Blick auf den Ukraine-Krieg und das Verhältnis zu Moskau. Die 62-jährige Jotowa unterstützt die EU- und Nato-Mitgliedschaft ihres Landes, lehnt Militärhilfen für die Ukraine aber ab. Im Wahlkampf inszenierte sie sich als „Präsidentin des Friedens“, die mit Moskau in einen Dialog treten will. Unmittelbar nach Bekanntwerden der Prognosen erklärte sich Jotowa zur Wahlsiegerin. Ihre Botschaft habe sich auf „Einkommen, Frieden und die vor uns liegenden Herausforderungen“ konzentriert, sagte sie an der Seite von Regierungschef Radew. Dieser gratulierte der von ihm unterstützten Kandidatin mit den Worten: „Heute hat sich das bulgarische Volk für die Zukunft und gegen die Vergangenheit entschieden.“ Auch EU-Kommissionspräsidentin Ursula von der Leyen gratulierte Jotowa. „Von Sicherheit und Verteidigung bis hin zu unserer Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Energieunabhängigkeit – ich freue mich darauf, unsere gemeinsame Arbeit fortzusetzen“, schrieb von der Leyen im Onlinedienst X. „Für ein starkes Bulgarien in einem starken Europa“, fügte sie hinzu. Wahl durch Drohnenangriffe überschattet Nach ihrer Stimmabgabe in Sofia hatte Jotowa gesagt, sie wolle, dass „Bulgarien in einem starken Europa stark ist“ und „souverän in seinen Entscheidungen“ bleibe. Der Oppositionskandidat Gjurow erklärte indes nach seiner Niederlage: „Wir haben ein solides Fundament gelegt, auf dem wir aufbauen können.“ Es sei nun wichtig, Einigkeit anzustreben. Überschattet wurde die Wahl durch mehrere Drohnenangriffe auf Handelsschiffe im Schwarzen Meer in den vergangenen Wochen. Gjurow hatte die Amtsinhaberin vor der Stichwahl dafür kritisiert, Russland nicht ausdrücklich für die Angriffe verantwortlich gemacht zu haben. Mutmaßlich im Zuge des Ukraine-Kriegs waren Anfang und Mitte Oktober vor der bulgarischen Schwarzmeerküste vier Handelsschiffe von Drohnen getroffen worden. 21 Menschen werden seitdem vermisst, sie sind vermutlich tot. Regierungschef Radew bestellte die russische Botschafterin ein, sah aber davon ab, offiziell einen Schuldigen zu benennen. Im ersten Wahlgang vor einer Woche hatte Jotowa mit 35 Prozent der Stimmen nur knapp vor Gjurow gelegen, der auf 32 Prozent kam. Damit schnitt die Amtsinhaberin deutlich schlechter ab als in Umfragen vorhergesagt. Jotowa, eine ehemalige Journalistin und sozialistische Europaabgeordnete, hatte das Präsidentenamt erst im Januar vom damaligen Amtsinhaber und heutigen Regierungschef Radew übernommen. Dieser war zurückgetreten und hatte anschließend die Parlamentswahl gewonnen und das Amt des Ministerpräsidenten übernommen. Die Regierung hatte im Juni Waffenlieferungen aus Beständen der bulgarischen Armee an die Ukraine gestoppt und sich später aus der internationalen „Koalition der Willigen“ zur Unterstützung Kiews zurückgezogen. Die bulgarische Rüstungsindustrie liefert allerdings weiterhin Waffen an Kiew. Das Balkanland mit seinen 6,4 Millionen Einwohnern hat traditionell enge Beziehungen zu Russland, ist in dieser Frage aber tief gespalten. Die Soziologin Borjana Dimitrowa vom Forschungsinstitut Alpha Research sagte, angesichts der Sorgen und Unsicherheiten in der Bevölkerung nach den Angriffen im Schwarzen Meer habe Jotowa die Wähler dadurch überzeugt, dass sie sich als „Friedens-Präsidentin“ präsentiert habe. „Die Angst vor dem Krieg wurde ausgenutzt.“ Für Radew und seine Partei sei die Wahl „entscheidend für die Stabilität ihres Machterhalts“ gewesen. Die Beteiligung im ersten Wahlgang hatte mit 23 Prozent einen historischen Tiefpunkt erreicht. In der Stichwahl lag sie laut ersten Prognosen mit zwischen 27 und 29 Prozent etwas höher. Im politischen System Bulgariens hat das Staatsoberhaupt vor allem repräsentative Aufgaben. Es kann allerdings sein Veto gegen Gesetze einlegen und ist Oberbefehlshaber der Streitkräfte des Nato-Mitgliedslandes.

welt.de.title: Unmittelbar nach den US-Kongresswahlen? Trump und Netanjahu beraten über neue Iran-Angriffe
welt.de.text: US-Präsident Donald Trump und der israelische Regierungschef Benjamin Netanjahu haben laut einem Medienbericht in einem Telefonat über mögliche neue Angriffe auf den Iran beraten. Bei dem Gespräch am Samstag hätten die beiden über den Stand der Vermittlungsbemühungen diskutiert, berichtete das Nachrichtenportal „Axios“ am Sonntag unter Berufung auf Regierungsbeamte beider Staaten. Netanjahu habe dazu gedrängt, den Iran unmittelbar nach den US-Kongresswahlen am Dienstag erneut anzugreifen, während Trump eine Fortsetzung der diplomatischen Bemühungen vorziehe. Der israelische Beamte bezeichnete das Gespräch demnach als „hart“, der US-Vertreter als „direkt“. Am Samstag hatte Trump vor Reportern gesagt, die diplomatischen Bemühungen um eine Verhandlungslösung zur Beendigung des Iran-Kriegs liefen „gut“. Gleichzeitig gebe es aber noch ein bis zwei mögliche Angriffsziele, um die sich die USA „kümmern“ müssten, darunter einen mutmaßlichen Atomkomplex südlich von Teheran. Der iranische Außenminister Abbas Araghtschi hatte gleichzeitig den Eingang eines Schreibens von US-Vizepräsident J.D. Vance bestätigt, in dem es laut einem Bericht des „Wall Street Journal“ um einen „möglichen Verhandlungsrahmen“ ging. Zuvor hatte Trump Teheran erneut gedroht  und mögliche neue Angriffe auf Ziele im Iran ins Spiel gebracht (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article6ae6a6596a5ed9f213134010/pickaxe-mountain-koennen-wir-in-zehn-minuten-erledigen-trump-nennt-weitere-angriffsziele-im-iran.html) . „Wir haben ihr Atomprogramm ausgeschaltet. Wir müssen uns noch um, ich würde sagen, ein oder zwei Anlagen kümmern, aber das können wir in zehn Minuten erledigen“, sagte Trump vor Journalisten auf seinem Anwesen Mar-a-Lago im US-Bundesstaat Florida. Konkret nannte Trump den iranischen Berg Kolang, auch als „Pickaxe Mountain“ bekannt, unter dem ein iranischer Atomkomplex vermutet wird. „Man könnte sich wahrscheinlich den Pickaxe Mountain ansehen, und darum muss man sich kümmern“, sagte Trump. Die USA und Israel hatten den Iran-Krieg Ende Februar mit Angriffen auf Ziele im Iran begonnen. Teheran reagierte mit Angriffen auf US-Ziele in der Region und auf mehrere Golfstaaten.

welt.de.title: Russlandfreundliche Präsidentin Jotowa liegt nach Prognosen in Bulgarien vorn
welt.de.text: Bei der Stichwahl um das  Präsidentenamt in Bulgarien (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article6ade74dbba080c37bf6d1583/eu-land-bulgaren-muessen-in-stichwahl-ueber-staatsoberhaupt-entscheiden.html)  deutet sich nach ersten Prognosen eine Mehrheit für Amtsinhaberin Ilijana Jotowa an. Wie aus Wählerbefragungen nach der Stimmabgabe des bulgarischen Meinungsforschungsinstituts Mjara hervorgeht, könnte Jotowa, die Kandidatin der regierenden Mitte-Links-Partei Progressives Bulgarien (PB), auf 51 Prozent der Stimmen kommen. Bei klarem Rückstand folgt den Angaben zufolge der prowestliche Herausforderer Andrej Gjurow mit knapp 45 Prozent. Der frühere Interimsregierungschef wird vom liberal-konservativen Oppositionslager unterstützt. Ukraine-Krieg prägt Wahl in Bulgarien Der Ukrainekrieg unweit von Bulgarien verleiht der Wahl in dem Land an der Ostflanke der Nato eine neue Dimension. Jotowa setzte sich im Wahlkampf immer wieder für eine Friedenslösung für die Ukraine durch Verhandlungen mit Russland ein. Sie sagte, sie wolle eine bulgarische „Präsidentin des Friedens“ sein. Gjurow ließ im Wahlkampf eine engere Orientierung an den westlichen Partnern erwarten sowie eine stärkere Unterstützung für die Ukraine im russischen Angriffskrieg. Die Wahl in dem südöstlichen EU-Land wurde von dem Konflikt überschattet. In der bulgarischen Wirtschaftszone im Schwarzen Meer – und auch in der des Nachbarlandes Rumänien – häuften sich in den vergangenen Wochen Drohnenangriffe auf Handelsschiffe. 6,5 Millionen Bürger konnten wählen Rund 6,5 Millionen Bulgaren konnten wählen. Die Wahlbeteiligung lag kurz vor Wahlschluss Meinungsforschern zufolge bei nur 29 Prozent. Damit war das Interesse an der Stichwahl aber größer als beim ersten Wahlgang vor einer Woche.

welt.de.title: Nach US-Warnung vor drohendem Anschlag in Moskau – Minderjähriger Russe festgenommen
welt.de.text: Nach einer US-Warnung vor einem womöglich geplanten Anschlag in Moskau haben die russischen Behörden einen Minderjährigen festgenommen. Es seien unter anderem auf der Internet-Plattform Tiktok Fotos des Verdächtigen in Kampfmontur und offenbar mit einer Waffe entdeckt worden, teilte am Sonntag der russische Inlandsgeheimdienst FSB mit. Die Ermittler hätten zudem auf seinem Handy „ein Abonnement eines neonazistischen Telegram-Kanals“ sowie in seinem Suchverlauf Recherchen zu terroristischen Anschlägen und Massenmorden gefunden. Bei der Festnahme des Teenagers seien in seiner Wohnung die genutzte Kleidung und die Gegenstände aus seiner vorherigen Veröffentlichung gefunden worden. Zudem habe der Verdächtige eine „bedeutende Zahl“ von Suchanfragen im Internet über „Terrorakte, Massenmorde und andere gewaltsame Aktionen“ abgesetzt. Der FSB hatte am Samstag mitgeteilt, dass er von den USA  über einen womöglich geplanten Anschlag unterrichtet worden sei (verlinkt auf https://www.welt.de/politik/ausland/article6ae60ca483885fcf33b05b38/terrorismus-zwischenfall-mit-massenhaften-verlusten-washington-warnt-moskau-vor-anschlag-auf-park.html) . Die US-Botschaft in Moskau sprach zeitgleich eine Sicherheitswarnung für das Zarizyno-Museum aus, eine Schloss- und Parkanlage im Süden von Moskau. Es gebe eine „glaubwürdige“ Bedrohungslage mit potenziell vielen Opfern. Im Zuge der Ermittlungen wurde laut FSB nun „ein minderjähriger russischer Staatsbürger“ festgenommen. Die von ihm selbst geposteten Fotos auf Tiktok zeigten ihn mit „taktischer Ausrüstung sowie einer Sturmhaube“ und „einem Gegenstand, der einer automatischen Waffe ähnelt“. Zudem seien Fotos entdeckt worden, die im Zarizyno-Museum aufgenommen wurden und mit der Bildunterschrift „Ich habe einen Ort gefunden“ versehen gewesen seien, erklärte der Geheimdienst laut russischen Staatsmedien. Warnung auch von der deutschen Botschaft Aufgrund des US-Hinweises wurden am Samstag alle Massenveranstaltungen im Park abgesagt und die Sicherheitsmaßnahmen verstärkt. Auch die deutsche Botschaft in Moskau hatte in einem Rundschreiben vor dem Besuch von Zarizyno gewarnt. „Wir danken der amerikanischen Seite für die bereitgestellte Information“, teilte der FSB mit. Die USA haben Russland in der Vergangenheit wiederholt vor drohenden Anschlägen gewarnt, unter anderem im März 2024, Wochen vor einem Anschlag auf eine Konzerthalle bei Moskau mit mehr als 140 Toten.

welt.de.title: „Wir Europäer zahlen den Preis für dieses Sanktionssystem“
welt.de.text: Russland müsse weiter hart sanktioniert werden, um den Ukraine-Krieg zu beenden, sagt der Berater des polnischen Präsidenten. In der Diskussion um Wiedergutmachung aus Deutschland lässt er sich vom Schicksal seiner Großmutter leiten.

sozcu.com.tr.title: Diyarbakır’da bir haftada 87 firari hükümlü yakalandı
sozcu.com.tr.text: Diyarbakır’da İl Jandarma Komutanlığı ekiplerince son bir haftada düzenlenen operasyonlarda 87 firari hükümlü yakalandı. Operasyonlar, Jandarma Suç Araştırma Timleri (JASAT) ile ilçe jandarma komutanlıkları tarafından gerçekleştirildi. Haklarında çeşitli suçlardan kesinleşmiş hapis cezası bulunan hükümlüler, işlemlerinin ardından adliyeye sevk edildi.

sozcu.com.tr.title: Duyan sokak sokak aramaya çıkıyor: Gramı bile 280 bin lira ediyor
sozcu.com.tr.text: Define avcılığının geleneksel sembolü olan altın, yerini uzaydan gelen nadir kalıntılara bırakıyor. Tarihi sikke ya da doğal külçe altın bulmak büyük bir kazanç olarak görülürken, aramalarda elde edilebilecek en yüksek maddi değere göktaşları ulaşıyor. Almanya'nın Oberwesel kentindeki göktaşı müzesinin direktörü ve uzmanı Stefan Decker, bu materyallerin piyasa değerinin kökenlerine ve yapısal niteliklerine göre belirlendiğini ifade etti. Decker’in paylaştığı verilere göre göktaşlarının gram fiyatı 1 euro (yaklaşık 56,10 TL) ile 5.000 euro (yaklaşık 280.500 TL) arasında değişkenlik gösteriyor. Piyasadaki 999 saflıktaki altının gramı yaklaşık 150 euro (yaklaşık 8.415 TL) seviyesinde seyrederken, saf ve büyük altın külçelerine doğada oldukça ender rastlanıyor. Bu durum, nitelikli bir göktaşı parçası bulmanın altın aramaya kıyasla daha yüksek bir kazanç potansiyeli taşıdığını gösteriyor. FİYATI VE DEĞERİ BELİRLEYEN KRİTERLER Yeryüzüne düşen her göktaşı yüksek meblağlarla alıcı bulmuyor. Bir parçanın değerlemesinde; kimyasal ve mineralojik bileşimi, fiziki aşınma durumu, düşüşünün üzerinden geçen zaman ve türün doğadaki nadirliği belirleyici rol oynuyor. Koleksiyonerler ile araştırma enstitüleri özellikle Ay ve Mars menşeli örnekler ile sıra dışı bileşenler barındıran taşları tercih ediyor. HUKUKİ MEVZUAT VE MÜLKİYET DURUMU Göktaşlarına dair yasal düzenlemeler ülkeden ülkeye farklılık arz ediyor. Örnek olarak Almanya mevzuatında düşen parça, onu bulan kişiye değil, arazinin mülkiyet sahibine ait sayılıyor. Bununla birlikte, bilimsel açıdan yüksek öneme sahip olduğu tespit edilen buluntuların kamu yararı gerekçesiyle devlet korumasına alınması veya müsadere edilmesi ihtimali de yasal çerçevede yer alıyor.

sozcu.com.tr.title: Amerikan askerleri ülkeyi birbirine kattı: Sokağa çıkma yasağı ilan ettiler
sozcu.com.tr.text: Güneydeki Okinawa Adası'nda bir kadını öldürmekle suçlanan 20 yaşındaki bir Amerikan deniz piyadesi hakkında iddianame hazırlanmasının hemen ardından, gece sokağa çıkma yasağını ihlal eden ikinci bir askerin alkollü araç kullanırken yakalanması bardağı taşıran son damla oldu. Yaşanan bu gelişmeler üzerine Japonya Savunma Bakanı Şinciro Koizumi, ABD yönetimine açık bir çağrıda bulunarak askeri personelin disipline edilmesi talebini iletti. CİNAYET TELEFON KABLOSU İLE İŞLENDİ Naha kentindeki bir otelde 3 Ekim günü gerçekleşen ve telefon kablosuyla işlenen cinayet vakası, Japon kamuoyunda büyük bir infiale yol açtı. Olayın ardından Japonya Başbakanı Sanae Takaiçi, parlamentoda yaptığı açıklamada ABD nezdinde en sert şekilde protesto girişiminde bulunulduğunu bildirdi. SOKAĞA ÇIKMA YASAĞI İLAN ETTİLER Başbakan Takaiçi, Washington'dan adli soruşturmayla tam iş birliği yapmasını ve üslerdeki askeri disiplinin tavizsiz şekilde sağlanmasını istedi. Cinayetin ardından Okinawa'daki ABD kuvvetlerine alkol yasağı getirilmiş ve gece yarısından sabah 05.00'e kadar süren 30 günlük sokağa çıkma kısıtlaması uygulanmaya başlanmıştı. Ancak alınan sıkı tedbirlere ve uygulanan sokağa çıkma yasağına rağmen ikinci bir askerin alkollü halde direksiyon başında yakalanması, adadaki Amerikan varlığına ilişkin tartışmaları yeniden alevlendirdi. Japonya Dışişleri Bakanı Toşimitsu Motegi, üs dışındaki davranış kurallarının baştan sona yeniden incelemeye alındığını duyurdu. Yaklaşık 54 bin Amerikan askerine ev sahipliği yapan ve bu gücün büyük kısmını bünyesinde barındıran Okinawa'da askerlerin karıştığı adli suçlar, iki müttefik ülke arasında kronik bir kriz alanı olmaya devam ediyor.

sozcu.com.tr.title: 270 liraya alıp 752 liraya satıyorlar: Üretici perişan
sozcu.com.tr.text: Türkiye Ziraat Odaları Birliği verilerine göre, ekim ayında kuru kayısının kilogram fiyatı üreticide 270 lira olarak kaydedildi. Aynı ürün pazarda 750 liradan, markette ise 752 liradan satışa sunuldu. Üretici ile market arasındaki fiyat farkı yüzde 178,7 olarak hesaplandı. Kuru kayısı, bu oranla 37 ürünün bulunduğu listede onuncu sırada yer aldı. ZİRAİ DONUN ETKİSİ SÜRÜYOR Kuru kayısı fiyatlarındaki yükselişte 12 Nisan 2025 tarihinde yaşanan zirai don felaketinin de etkisi bulunuyor. Özellikle kayısı üretiminin yoğun olduğu bölgelerde yaşanan don, ağaçlarda ve ürün miktarında kayıplara yol açtı. Üretim sürecinde hava koşullarıyla mücadele eden çiftçiler, hasat ettikleri ürünü belirli bir fiyattan satarken market raflarında çok daha yüksek rakamlarla karşılaşılıyor. Üreticide 270 lira olan kuru kayısının tüketiciye 752 liradan ulaşması, tarladan sofraya uzanan zincirde fiyat farkının en çok hangi aşamada oluştuğu sorusunu gündeme taşıdı.

sozcu.com.tr.title: Borsa günün ilk yarısında pozitif seyretti -2 Kasım 2026
sozcu.com.tr.text: Günün ilk yarısında yükseliş eğiliminde hareket eden BIST 100 endeksi, saat 13.00 itibarıyla önceki kapanışa göre 75,38 puan ve yüzde 0,70 artışla 10.834,94 puana çıktı. Toplam işlem hacmi 49,6 milyar lira oldu. Bankacılık endeksi yüzde 2,35, holding endeksi yüzde 0,17 değer kazandı. Sektör endeksleri arasında en çok kazandıran yüzde 3,81 ile ulaştırma, en fazla kaybettiren ise yüzde 4,02 ile finansal kiralama faktoring oldu. Küresel piyasalarda, ABD-İran görüşmelerine ilişkin iyimserlikle gerileyen petrol fiyatları risk iştahını desteklerken ABD'de devam eden seçim sürecine ve yapay zeka yatırımlarının karlılığına ilişkin endişeler nedeniyle temkinli bir seyir izleniyor. Analistler, günün geri kalanında imalat sanayi Satınalma Yöneticileri Endeksi (PMI), haftalık para ve banka istatistiklerinin, yurt dışında dünya genelinde açıklanacak imalat sanayi PMI verilerinin takip edileceğini belirterek, teknik açıdan BIST 100 endeksinde 11.000 ve 11.100 puanın direnç, 10.700 ve 10.600 puanın destek konumunda olduğunu kaydetti.

sozcu.com.tr.title: Bir zamanlar gökyüzüne hükmeden, insan avlayan dev kartallar çok önemli bir görev üstlenmiş
sozcu.com.tr.text: Güney Afrika'da 2,8 milyon yıl önce yaşayan, yaklaşık üç yaşındaki bir çocuğun kalıntıları, insan atalarının yalnızca avcı değil, av da olduğunu gösteriyor. “Taung çocuğu” olarak bilinen Australopithecus africanus yavrusunun göz çukurlarının hemen altındaki delinme izleri, kartalların avlarında bıraktığı izlerle örtüşüyor. Çocuğu öldüren kuşun hangi tür olduğu kesin olarak bilinmiyor. Ancak fosildeki hasarla günümüzde kartalların avladığı primatların kemiklerindeki benzerlik, gökyüzünden gelen tehlikenin somut kanıtları arasında yer alıyor. BBC Türkçe'nin aktardığı uzman değerlendirmelerine göre bu tehlike, insan atalarının bedenlerini ve sosyal davranışlarını şekillendiren evrimsel baskılardan biri olmuş olabilir. 600'DEN FAZLA PRİMATIN KALINTILARI İNCELENDİ ABD'deki Ohio Eyalet Üniversitesi'nden primatolog Scott McGraw, Fildişi Sahili'ndeki Taï Ormanı'nda, Afrika taçlı kartalları gibi yırtıcı kuşların öldürdüğü 600'den fazla primata ait kalıntıları inceledi. Bazı kafataslarının göz çukuru tabanındaki hasar, Taung çocuğundaki izlerle çarpıcı benzerlik taşıyordu. McGraw, karşılaştırmanın nasıl yapıldığını şöyle anlatıyor: “Çalışmamızı değerlendiren hakemlerden biri fosil deposuna gidip Taung Çocuğu'nu incelediğinde, söz konusu hasarın birebir aynı olduğunu gördü.” İnsan atalarının yırtıcı kuşlar tarafından düzenli olarak avlandığı görüşünü savunan McGraw'a göre, geçmişte toplanan insan fosillerinin yeniden incelenmesiyle benzer saldırılara ait başka izler de bulunabilir. İngiltere'deki Brighton Üniversitesi'nden arkeolog ve uygulamalı bilimler uzmanı James Cole da erken insan atalarının kuşlardan leoparlara, sırtlanlardan dev timsahlara kadar çeşitli yırtıcıların avı olduğunu belirtiyor. “KALABALIKTA GÜVENLİK VARDIR” Bu yırtıcılardan kaçınma ihtiyacının, iki ayak üzerinde durarak çevreyi daha kolay gözlemlemekten iş birliği ve birbirini korumaya kadar farklı özelliklerin gelişimine katkıda bulunmuş olabileceği düşünülüyor. Cole, grup büyüklüğünün önemini “Kalabalıkta güvenlik vardır” sözleriyle vurguluyor. McGraw da özellikle yırtıcı kuşlardan korunmada büyük sosyal grupların avantaj sağladığını belirtiyor. Taçlı kartallar gibi kuşlar, avlarını uzun süre kovalamak yerine ağaçların arasında gizlenip uygun anda saldırabiliyor. Grup içindeki çok sayıda bireyin çevreyi gözetlemesi, bu ani saldırıların fark edilmesini kolaylaştırabiliyor. Bu durum “çoklu göz etkisi” olarak adlandırılıyor. Cole'a göre büyüyen gruplarda işlerin ve rollerin ayrışması, görüş mesafesinin ötesinde de koordinasyon ihtiyacı doğurmuş ve dilin ortaya çıkışına katkı sağlamış olabilir. McGraw ise primatların yırtıcı kuşlar için özel sesli uyarılar kullanmasının, dilin öncüsü olarak yorumlanabileceğini söylüyor. ALTI METRELİK KANAT AÇIKLIĞINA SAHİP YIRTICILAR İnsanlarla dev kuşların karşılaşmaları yalnızca Afrika'yla sınırlı değildi. Amerika kıtasına ulaşan ilk insanlar, altı metreye varan kanat açıklıklarına sahip teratornlarla karşılaşmış olabilir. Akbabaları andıran bu kuşlar hem leşle besleniyor hem de avlanıyordu. Güney Kaliforniya ve Nevada'da yaşayan Aiolornis incredibilis'in kanat açıklığı beş buçuk metreye ulaşırken, Oregon'daki Teratornis woodburnensis'in kanat açıklığı dört metreydi. Yaklaşık 12 bin yıl önce de varlığını sürdüren bu ikinci türün fosilleri; mamutlar, mastodonlar, dev tembel hayvanlar ve ilk insanların kalıntılarıyla birlikte bulundu. Londra Doğa Tarihi Müzesi kuş anatomisi koleksiyonları kıdemli küratörü Joanne Cooper, teratornların Kuzey Amerika yerli kültürlerindeki Thunderbird efsanelerine ilham vermiş olabileceğini belirtiyor. HAAST KARTALI: “ADETA UÇAN BİR KAPLAN” Yeni Zelanda'daki Maori anlatılarında çocukları kapıp götüren dev kuş Te Hokioi'nin de soyu tükenmiş Haast kartalına dayandığı düşünülüyor. Cooper'ın “adeta uçan bir kaplan” diye tanımladığı Haast kartalı, günümüzdeki en büyük kartal türlerinden harpi kartalının yaklaşık iki katı ağırlığındaydı. Dört metre boyundaki, yerde yaşayan moa kuşlarıyla besleniyor; 10 santimetrelik pençeleriyle avını yere seriyordu. Moa leğen kemiklerinde bu pençelerin izlerinin görüldüğünü belirten Cooper, Haast kartalının insanlara saldırabilecek yetenekte olduğunu da değerlendiriyor: “Çocuklar kesinlikle risk altındaydı. Bu hem hayranlık uyandırıcı hem de dehşet verici bir durum olmalı.” Dev hayvanların yok oluşunda iklim değişikliğinin ve insan avcılığının ne ölçüde rol oynadığı ise kesinlik kazanmış değil. İnsanların yayılması ve ekosistemlerde yarattığı değişimler, megafaunanın yüzde 95'e varan oranda yok olmasıyla eş zamanlı yaşandı.
